findings.reason: the section must either become two sections (with the catch-up owning its read record) or drop the views clause back to "launch does not wait on the session".
findings.text: §5 now delivers two behaviours: a watch-stream row written within the admit pass that launches a queued request, and a catch-up in the live and obligations views that lists runs submitted since the session's previous read and drops them on the following read. The second needs per-session read bookkeeping that the system does not have and that §5 gives one line and one hour to, so a single verdict cannot close both and the gate proves neither

findings.reason: the assertion must name every field the deliverable requires, or the key field (the `crew tell` command) can be missing from a passing run.
findings.text: the changed §5 done-when asserts each row names "its run, section, lane and advice", but the deliverable also requires the plan, the model and the `crew tell` command that reaches the worker. A node can satisfy the gate while the row omits the steering handle, which is the only reason the section exists

findings.reason: without a control for the views clause the node cannot show that half of its deliverable is guarded, which is exactly the gap the earlier review closed for the row.
findings.text: the negative control named for §5 ("removing the row write from the launch path makes the two-row assertion fail") falsifies only the watch-row half; the added views assertions have no mutation that shows them failing, so a view that lists all live runs rather than runs submitted since the session's previous read could pass the first read and still be indistinguishable from the intended behaviour except through the second read alone

findings.reason: the author must either name where the read record lives and who writes it, or restate the clause as "the views list the run once it is live, however long the session was away", which needs no new state.
findings.text: §5 says "its live and obligations views list every run submitted since it last read them", but no record of a session's previous read exists: the views are built on demand (`view="live"` in `reckon/crew/query.py`, the obligations snapshot in `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py`), and reading them writes nothing. The endpoint is therefore not obtainable from the system as described, and the done-when's "neither on the read after that" cannot hold without a persisted cursor that the plan assigns to no one
